sourceFacts: Most Down syndrome results from three copies of chromosome21.
Other forms involve translocation or mosaicism, so this diagram specifically depicts free trisomy.
prompt:
Create a polished original medical teaching illustration in landscape 3:2 format. Use the attached MD3 original solely as a style reference: warm watercolour/gouache on an ivory paper background, delicate ink contours, calm navy labels, muted ochre/peach/teal colours, generous whitespace and clear flat anatomical shapes. Anatomical clarity before decoration. Never photorealistic skin, glossy blood, wet flesh, fat lobules, scary faces, chunky 3D tissue blocks, or a fake scan. Only exact requested labels, clean legible short text. Footer 'Educational schematic'. No watermark, logos or attribution in the pixels. Compose an entirely new subject from the clinical specification, not the scalp content in the reference.

Two clear chromosome-count groups on warm ivory background. Title 'Trisomy 21: an extra copy'. Left heading 'Two copies': EXACTLY TWO small matching acrocentric chromosome21 symbols, each with a tiny short arm above high centromere and long arms below; both muted teal. Right heading 'Three copies': EXACTLY THREE matching chromosome21 symbols; two muted teal and third pale ochre. Label below each group 'Chromosome 21'. Bottom 'The common free-trisomy form of Down syndrome'. No full karyotype, no infant faces, no physically different third chromosome, no duplicated chromosome arms miscounted as chromosomes. Small subtitle 'Copy-number schematic'. All chromosome symbols same size and shape, distinct separated silhouettes.
